fixes: Set tariff.VERSION and the pyproject version to 2.4.1, requires-python to >=3.12, and emptied the dependencies list so the package is standard library only.
Fixed the tier split in core.rate_tiers: tier 1 now covers 0 up to and including its up_to and each later tier starts at the previous up_to instead of one unit below it.
Prorated the standing charge over the days of the account's billing period instead of a fixed 30-day month in core.standing_line.
Computed every amount with decimal.Decimal from the values as written in the input files and rounded each line amount half to even to 0.01, emitting amounts as two-decimal strings.
Rewrote core.settle so the commitment credit is tested against the invoice subtotal and the total is subtotal x (1 - credit_rate) rounded half to even, with credit = subtotal - total.
Dropped the bogus 'base' charge that rated rejected reads, so the credit no longer counts unaccepted consumption.
Rejected text quantities in parser._quantity: only a JSON integer of 0 or more is accepted, so strings, decimals, exponents, booleans and null are malformed_quantity.
Added the missing outside_period exception in parser.classify, in its contract position after inactive_meter and before duplicate_read.
Sorted the exception list by read_id in ascending string order instead of by account.
Made python -m tariff report the first missing input file on standard error and exit 2.
Corrected the README and the docstrings that described a 30-day proration and a consumption-based credit base.
Corrected the two visible tests that asserted the 30-day proration and the old credit base.
